title: Render a Greeting
question: Return an <h1> element that displays the text: Hello, React!
constraints: Use JSX. Return a single <h1> element.
hints: JSX looks like HTML but is JavaScript.
Return the element directly from the component.
optimized: Same — this is a fundamentals check.

discussion.whyAsked: Confirms you understand components return JSX.
discussion.mistakes: Returning a string instead of JSX; forgetting the component must return something.
followUps: Why must there be a single root element?

title: Build a Counter
question: Add state with useState and make the button increment the count shown in the <h2>.
constraints: Use the useState hook. Do not mutate a plain variable.
hints: Call setCount in the button's onClick.
bruteForce: A plain variable won't re-render the UI.
optimized: useState triggers a re-render when the value changes.

discussion.mistakes: Using a normal variable; mutating it instead of calling the setter.
followUps: Why doesn't a normal variable work?
What if you click +1 three times in one handler?

title: Toggle ON / OFF
question: Make the button toggle the heading between 'OFF' and 'ON' using a boolean state.
constraints: Use a boolean state and the functional updater.
bruteForce: Tracking a string works but a boolean is cleaner.

discussion.mistakes: Mutating state; forgetting to read it in the JSX.
followUps: Why use the functional updater here?

title: Render a List
question: Render the fruits array as a <ul> of <li> items, each with a stable key.
constraints: Use .map and provide a key prop.
hints: key should be a stable unique value, not the array index when the list can reorder.
optimized: Map over the array so it scales with the data.

discussion.whyAsked: Lists + keys are asked in almost every React interview.
discussion.mistakes: Missing key; using the index as key in a reorderable list.

title: Double the Value
question: Start the value at 1 and make the button double it on each click.
constraints: Use the functional updater since the next value depends on the previous.
bruteForce: setValue(value * 2) works for one click but is unsafe under batching.
optimized: Functional updater always uses the latest value.

discussion.mistakes: Reading stale state in rapid updates.
followUps: When must you use the functional updater?

title: Increment by 3 (Functional Updates)
question: Clicking the button should increase the count by 3 in a SINGLE click. The naive version only adds 1 — fix it.
constraints: Do not change the number of setCount calls — only how they compute the next value.
hints: All three calls read the same captured count.
bruteForce: setCount(count + 1) x3 all see the same count and add 1.
optimized: Functional updaters queue and compose, adding 3.

discussion.mistakes: Not understanding that count is captured per render.
followUps: Why does the naive version add only 1?
Does React 18 batch outside event handlers?

title: Controlled Input with Live Count
question: Make the input controlled and show the live character count below it.
constraints: value must come from state; the count is derived (not its own state).
bruteForce: Storing the count separately risks drift.
optimized: Derive the count from the text state.

discussion.mistakes: Uncontrolled input; storing the count in separate state.

title: Show Only Active Users
question: Render only the users whose active flag is true, as <li> items with a stable key.
constraints: Filter then map; use a stable key (id).
bruteForce: Rendering all then hiding inactive with CSS still mounts them.
optimized: Filter the data so only active users render.

discussion.mistakes: Using array index as key; forgetting to filter.
followUps: Why is id a better key than index here?
